Precinct Targets · where votes can still be picked up

Texas 2026 general · early voting through Oct 25 (day 7) · nine counties · built Oct 26, 9:59 AM from the state's downloaded voter lists and county check-in lists, the state's primary and general rosters by voter ID, and the Texas Legislative Council's precinct results and registration.

Democratic base still out (the chase universe)People who voted in a Democratic primary or runoff in 2022, 2024 or 2026 and never in a Republican one, counted in the precinct of their most recent record, who have not yet shown up on any 2026 early-voting list in Texas. The likeliest Democratic votes still out. The count splits into people who voted in a 2026 primary (current, most reliable) and people seen only in 2022 to 2024 (some have moved).
No-party regular voters still outPeople with no primary history who voted in the 2022 or 2024 general election and have not voted yet. They do turn out, but the data cannot say how they vote: the precinct's 2022 and 2024 results, shown beside every count, are the best guide.
Rarely-vote registered votersPeople on the November 2024 rolls who did not vote in the 2024 general and have no other record in the state's 2022 to 2026 rosters, minus any who have voted early this year. The biggest pool and the hardest to move, and an upper bound: it still includes people on the rolls who have since moved. Large numbers in Democratic-leaning precincts are the long-shot upside.
Total potentialThe three groups added together. They do not overlap, so the total is everyone in the precinct who could still vote. Start with the Democratic base, then the regulars in precincts that lean Democratic, then the rarely-vote pool where there is capacity.
How to use it: pick a county, then a view. The map colours every precinct; hover or click a precinct for its numbers; the table and the top-5 lists follow the county tab and the day slider. "Rank by" changes the lists and the table sort. The CSV in the same folder has every precinct and column.

Notes. Registered voters and the 2024 turnout per precinct are the state's November 2024 figures. Precincts created or renumbered since 2024 have no boundary on the map yet (Fort Bend and Tarrant renumbered many); they stay in the table and the rankings, marked "no boundary". The state's 2022 and 2024 Election Day rosters carry no county, so the 2022 to 2024-only part of the Democratic base and the regular-voter group are undercounts; the 2026-primary part is complete. Primary history covers 2022 to 2026 (2020 is not available). Mail voters count in their precinct. The chase universe drops anyone who has already voted in another county.
Sources: Texas SOS early-voting lists and county check-in lists (2026), SOS primary and general rosters 2022 to 2026 by voter ID, Texas Legislative Council precinct boundaries and 2022/2024 precinct returns and registration. Counts only; no voter names or IDs on this page.
